name: field prime
definition: Coordinates lie in the finite field \(\mathbb F_p\), the integers modulo \(p\). For secp256k1, \(p=2^{256}-2^{32}-977\). This modulus controls coordinate arithmetic.

name: local error probability
definition: On architecture and state-preparation pages, \(p\) is the error probability specified beside the formula: for example, a physical two-qubit Pauli error rate or an injected-state fault rate. Each model defines the event and operation counted. Arithmetic pages instead use \(p\) for the field prime.

name: subgroup order
definition: The number of distinct multiples of the generator point \(P\); \([r]P=\mathcal O\). Scalar recovery is modulo \(r\), not the field prime \(p\).

name: secret scalar
definition: The unknown element of \(\mathbb Z_r\) satisfying \(Q=[d]P\). Recovering it is the elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem.

name: curve points
definition: \(P\) is the chosen generator, \(Q\) is the public input point, and \(\mathcal O\) is the identity element of the curve group. \([a]P\) denotes repeated point addition.

name: small prime offset
definition: \(p=2^n-c\), so \(2^n\equiv c\pmod p\). For secp256k1, \(n=256\) and \(c=2^{32}+977\). This relation makes reduction of high bits cheap.

name: scalar-window width
definition: The number of scalar bits handled by one coherent point lookup. The main loop uses \(w=16\), giving tables indexed by 16-bit addresses.

name: point-addition slope
definition: For distinct affine points with different x coordinates, \(\lambda=(y_2-y_1)/(x_2-x_1)\) in \(\mathbb F_p\). The division means multiplication by a modular inverse. Elsewhere the same Greek letter may denote a Poisson mean; each lesson specifies its domain.

name: approximate-oracle failure bound
definition: For each fixed input pair, an upper bound over fresh random masks on producing either wrong coordinates or a wrong relative phase. Appendix B obtains \(p_f\le0.03346\).

name: ideal algorithm success
definition: Success probability assigned to exact arithmetic with the selected quantum Fourier measurement and classical recovery procedure. The rigorous and heuristic starting estimates must be kept separate.

name: quantum Fourier transform
definition: A unitary change of basis between a modular coordinate and its phase frequency. iQFT denotes its inverse. Measuring the result exposes the periodic relation used to recover the secret scalar.

name: Toffoli gate
definition: The three-bit reversible map \((a,b,t)\mapsto(a,b,t\oplus ab)\). It is a controlled-controlled-X gate and the main non-Clifford logical resource of the arithmetic.

name: controlled-controlled-Z
definition: The three-qubit unitary \(|a,b,c\rangle\mapsto(-1)^{abc}|a,b,c\rangle\). Conjugating its third qubit by Hadamards gives a Toffoli. A CCZ resource state is \(\mathrm{CCZ}|+\rangle^{\otimes3}\).

name: pi-over-four phase gate
definition: \(T=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\pi/4})\). A T state, up to the convention specified in a lesson, supplies this non-Clifford phase through state injection. The symbol \(T\) also denotes time in resource equations, where units are explicit.

name: tracked logical transformation
definition: A Clifford unitary maps Pauli operators to Pauli operators by conjugation. Instead of applying every such gate physically, the controller can track the accumulated map and reinterpret later measurements.

name: Clifford noise-reduction protocol
definition: Logical CliNR uses a prepared, checked Clifford resource and teleportation. Here it is used to clear a complicated tracked Clifford frame and restore simple logical-measurement representatives.

name: main memory code
definition: The quantum code \([[102,22,9]]\): 102 data qubits encode 22 logical qubits with distance 9. Device counts additionally include syndrome ancillas and replacement ions.

name: factory code
definition: The quantum code \([[66,4,10]]\): 66 data qubits encode four logical qubits with distance 10. It protects the CCZ-factory state and supports the specific representatives tabulated in Appendix G.

name: six-qubit detection code
definition: The \([[6,2,2]]\) code encodes two logical qubits. In the factory it prepares a pair of low-error logical H states using error detection and postselection.

name: shared parity-measurement resource
definition: A length-m cat is \((|0\rangle^{\otimes m}+|1\rangle^{\otimes m})/\sqrt2\). Each cat qubit touches at most one target qubit when measuring a product Pauli operator, limiting fault spread.

name: physical operation cycle
definition: The basic physical timing unit used in the architecture, \(0.2\,\mathrm{ms}\). Gate, transport, and syndrome schedules are expressed in these units.

name: syndrome-extraction cycle
definition: One repeated measurement of the code's error checks with its physical schedule. Q102 takes 27 POCs per SEC; Q66 takes 17 POCs per SEC under the stated architecture.

name: logical measurement
definition: LM denotes a measurement of a logical Pauli operator. LM2 spans two code blocks and requires resources that join their local cat states. A logical operation can take several SECs to achieve enough readout confidence.

name: Pauli support
definition: The physical qubits on which a Pauli string \(P\) acts as X, Y, or Z rather than I. Its cardinality is the operator weight. Commuting operators need not have disjoint supports.

name: physical realization of an encoded Pauli
definition: Different physical Pauli strings can implement the same logical operation because multiplying by a stabilizer leaves the encoded action unchanged. Choosing representatives controls weight and parallel compatibility.

name: greatest common divisor
definition: The largest integer dividing two inputs. Binary-gcd updates use parity tests, subtraction, and division by two. Recording and replaying these updates implements modular multiplication or division reversibly.

name: truncated carry width
definition: The number of low bits through which a small modular correction is allowed to propagate. A carry beyond that range is one of the approximate arithmetic failure events.

name: charged measurement depth
definition: The sum of scheduled logical-measurement layers, including the expected penalties used in the resource accounting: 75,251,329 for the reported computation.

name: seconds per charged layer
definition: Appendix E23 uses the unrounded value \(0.0294958\,\mathrm{s}\). Table I displays it as 29.50 ms. Runtime is \(D_{\rm meas}\tau\).

name: accept only verified preparations
definition: A preparation attempt is retained only if specified measurement checks pass; otherwise it restarts. Output error is conditioned on acceptance, and retries affect throughput.

name: survivor-displacement probability
definition: Conditional on a two-qubit interaction involving a loss, the probability that the surviving ion is displaced to the other position. It is not the ordinary two-qubit Pauli error probability.
